system-text-json-required-members.title: Understand required members with System.Text.Json
system-text-json-required-members.short: Treat missing required JSON members as a contract violation
system-text-json-required-members.summary: Types with required members can combine C# construction requirements with JSON contracts so missing critical data is detected near deserialization.
system-text-json-required-members.why: Letting missing values survive as nulls or defaults moves configuration and DTO failures far away from the input boundary.
system-text-json-required-members.tips: Use required only for genuinely mandatory contract data and check compatibility with existing payloads and custom JsonTypeInfo configuration.

file-stream-buffering-strategy.title: Choose FileStream buffering for the access pattern
file-stream-buffering-strategy.short: Avoid accidental double buffering and undersized I/O operations
file-stream-buffering-strategy.summary: FileStream buffering can combine small operations, but the useful configuration depends on upper-layer buffering, RandomAccess usage, and the actual I/O pattern.
file-stream-buffering-strategy.why: A larger buffer is not automatically faster and can add copies or memory consumption under concurrency.
file-stream-buffering-strategy.tips: Measure real operation sizes and concurrency, account for the OS cache, and give each buffering layer a clear purpose.

cancellationtoken-register-callback-cost.title: Manage CancellationToken.Register count and lifetime
cancellationtoken-register-callback-cost.short: Do not create unnecessary callback registrations in fine-grained loops
cancellationtoken-register-callback-cost.summary: Cancellation callbacks create registrations that must be tracked, so large numbers attached to long-lived tokens can accumulate allocation and cleanup work.
cancellationtoken-register-callback-cost.why: Registering unconditionally for every item pays management cost even on the normal path where cancellation never occurs.
cancellationtoken-register-callback-cost.tips: Register only at boundaries that need a callback and dispose each registration with the lifetime of its owner.

dictionary-alternate-lookup-span.title: Avoid temporary keys with Dictionary alternate lookup
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span.short: Supported comparers can query a dictionary through another key representation
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span.summary: For supported dictionary and comparer combinations, alternate lookup can search from representations such as spans without first materializing a temporary key object.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span.why: In hot string lookup paths, repeatedly constructing strings can make allocation and GC more expensive than the lookup itself.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span.tips: Check runtime and comparer support, and benchmark whether the extra complexity improves the actual workload over ordinary TryGetValue.

socket-keepalive-application-heartbeat.title: Separate socket keepalive from application heartbeats
socket-keepalive-application-heartbeat.short: Transport liveness and protocol liveness answer different questions
socket-keepalive-application-heartbeat.summary: TCP keepalive can help detect some dead connections, but it does not express whether an application peer is responsive or making protocol-level progress.
socket-keepalive-application-heartbeat.why: Relying on keepalive alone can leave a logically stalled peer considered healthy for much longer than the application can tolerate.
socket-keepalive-application-heartbeat.tips: Define the required detection time and semantics, then divide responsibility between transport keepalive, application heartbeat, and timeouts.

aspnetcore-request-aborted-propagation.title: Propagate ASP.NET Core RequestAborted downstream
aspnetcore-request-aborted-propagation.short: Stop unnecessary I/O and work after the client disconnects
aspnetcore-request-aborted-propagation.summary: HttpContext.RequestAborted represents request cancellation and can be passed as a CancellationToken to downstream operations that support cancellation.
aspnetcore-request-aborted-propagation.why: Dropping the token can leave database, HTTP, or expensive work consuming resources after the requesting client has gone away.
aspnetcore-request-aborted-propagation.tips: Propagate cancellation consistently through cancellable boundaries while separating cleanup or commit work that must finish even after request cancellation.

reflection-generic-constraint-validation.title: Handle generic constraint failures in reflection
reflection-generic-constraint-validation.short: MakeGenericType rejects type arguments that violate where constraints
reflection-generic-constraint-validation.summary: When reflection closes an open generic type, runtime validation still enforces class, struct, base-type, interface, and other generic constraints.
reflection-generic-constraint-validation.why: Systems that feed arbitrary Type values into MakeGenericType can fail only for particular plugins or runtime-selected types.
reflection-generic-constraint-validation.tips: Validate constraints when selecting external types or handle ArgumentException at the type-construction boundary.

eventcounter-observer-overhead.title: Measure the overhead of diagnostic counter observation
eventcounter-observer-overhead.short: Diagnostics can perturb the workload they are measuring
eventcounter-observer-overhead.summary: Runtime counters and diagnostic providers are valuable, but enabling more sources or collecting more frequently increases work in the observer and sometimes the target process.
eventcounter-observer-overhead.why: Heavy instrumentation used to investigate a performance issue can create behavior that differs from the unobserved production workload.
eventcounter-observer-overhead.tips: Enable only the providers and counters needed, choose an appropriate interval, and compare runs with and without observation when precision matters.

unity-physics-fixedupdate-timestep.title: Understand Unity physics and the FixedUpdate timestep
unity-physics-fixedupdate-timestep.short: Rendering frames and physics steps are separate timelines
unity-physics-fixedupdate-timestep.summary: Unity physics advances around a fixed timestep, so physics work should not be treated as if it runs once for every rendered Update frame.
unity-physics-fixedupdate-timestep.why: Applying frame-based assumptions directly to physics can make forces or movement depend on rendering frame rate.
unity-physics-fixedupdate-timestep.tips: Place physics operations with FixedUpdate semantics in mind and measure both stability and CPU cost before changing the fixed timestep.

async-dispose-exception-boundary.title: Account for exceptions from DisposeAsync
async-dispose-exception-boundary.short: The end of an await using scope can itself perform failing asynchronous work
async-dispose-exception-boundary.summary: IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync may flush or close asynchronous resources and can therefore fail while control is leaving an await using scope.
async-dispose-exception-boundary.why: Treating only the main body as the failure boundary misses errors that occur during resource finalization after otherwise successful work.
async-dispose-exception-boundary.tips: For resources where disposal failure matters, define how it interacts with body failures and logging rather than silently swallowing it.
